Virginia and Oregon filed lawsuits on Monday alleging that SpaceX, which acquired xAI in February, failed to stop Grok from generating non‑consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material.
The complaints claim the companies misled users about safety measures and continued to allow the model to produce such content.
Attorneys general say the lack of safeguards puts children at risk of lifelong distress.
The lawsuits describe Grok’s “spicy mode” as a feature that produced nude images without prompting, despite promises of added safeguards after early failures.
State officials allege that X Safety’s red‑team was reduced to two or three members, far below industry standards, and that the firms prioritized market share over safety.
They also note that Grok’s integration with the X platform could expose users as young as 13 to harmful content, potentially re‑traumatizing victims of abuse.
Grok is an AI image generator owned by xAI, now part of SpaceX after the February acquisition.

Earlier in its rollout, the model’s “spicy mode” was promoted by Elon Musk but quickly generated a flood of non‑consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse images, prompting public backlash and calls for stricter controls.

Anthropic announced Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents that automate code reviews, fixes, and approvals for routine changes on 23 November 2026.
The offering includes the existing Code Review tool and two new beta agents called PR Steward and Claude Approvals.
Claude Ship is available in beta, letting early adopters test the agents on pull requests before full deployment.

PR Steward intervenes when continuous‑integration (CI) checks fail, when merge conflicts arise, or when feedback from Code Review or teammates is present, and it leaves comments describing its changes and rollback steps.
Claude Approvals applies a policy file written by the team, using signals such as Code Review findings or custom classifiers, to automatically approve routine pull requests.
Anthropic recommends running approvals in observe‑only mode first and allows teams to limit spending and restrict the agents to specific repositories.
AI coding assistants have been generating large volumes of code, creating bottlenecks in manual review and approval processes.

Claude Ship extends Anthropic's earlier Code Review feature, which launched in March and became generally available in October 2026, by adding automation that can both fix issues and grant approvals under defined policies.
This reflects a broader trend of delegating more development workflow steps to AI while keeping human oversight options available.

President Donald Trump intervened to restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive after Huang resigned amid scandal, and the board voted unanimously to reinstate him on 23 November 2026.
Trump said he spoke directly with the board and used Vice President JD Vance as a liaison to assure no security risk.
The move surprised analysts and investors given the board’s earlier decision to bar Huang.
Trump appeared on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show and told listeners that Huang would “end up on his feet,” even suggesting Apple’s former CEO Tim Cook as a possible replacement.

Behind the scenes the White House communications director Steven Cheung confirmed Trump’s total involvement in the board’s reversal, and Trump reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to argue for Huang’s return.
The board’s unanimous vote reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and board director less than two weeks after his resignation, citing input from senior U.S. government officials.
Nvidia has become a central player in the Trump administration’s AI strategy, providing hardware for government projects and financing other AI firms with its $4 trillion‑plus market value.

Amazon announced it will buy Israeli startup Decart for $7.5 billion, according to Bloomberg.
The deal includes Decart’s Optimization Stack software, its founding team and AI engineers.
Amazon said the acquisition will help customers run AI workloads more efficiently on its Trainium chips and other hardware platforms.

entries.text: Decart is known for interactive real‑time world models such as Oasis 3 and AI video‑generation tools.
Its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) improves model efficiency on Nvidia, Amazon and Google hardware.
Peter DeSantis, Amazon’s SVP of foundational AI models, said more efficient compute leads to better training, reinforcement learning, inference and lower costs.
Amazon plans to sell Trainium chips to external customers, positioning them against Nvidia’s offerings.

Google announced that Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode can now connect to Google Wallet and Google Drive, with the Gemini app support arriving in the coming weeks.
Users may opt in through Search Personalization settings, keeping control over which apps share data.
The rollout began on 23 November 2026, starting with Wallet integration and expanding to Drive shortly after.
When users enable the feature, Search can draw on spending data from Google Wallet to highlight financial habits, suggest ways to trim everyday expenses, and optimize credit‑card rewards.
Connecting Google Drive lets Search reference documents, spreadsheets, and other files to generate personalized project plans or research summaries without repeated prompts.
The Gemini app will also feed chat context into Search, further enriching answers, and all connections remain optional and reversible at any time.
Personal Intelligence is Google’s effort to make Search responses context‑aware by leveraging data already stored in its ecosystem, such as Gmail, Calendar, and Photos.
By adding Wallet and Drive, Google extends this personalization to financial and document domains, aiming to reduce the need for users to manually retrieve information across apps.
The approach emphasizes user consent, with clear settings to manage data sharing and the ability to disable the AI mode entirely.
